blocks.orig: If there is one country where you can experience an authentic African safari, it is Tanzania. Boasting an awe-inspiring mix of wildlife, landscapes and culture, a Tanzania travel adventure is a memory that will last a lifetime. With magnificent national parks and protected game reserves accounting for 35% of the country, a Tanzania safari is a chance to see nature at its finest. Countless wild animals roam the lush landscapes, from elephants to lions – and there are few more incredible sights than the Great Wildebeest Migration in the Serengeti. In search of fresh water and grass, millions of mammals follow the rainfall in a clockwise circle every year.
blocks.html: Tanzania is the country for a genuine African safari, if ever there was one. With its breathtaking blend of wildlife, scenery and culture, a trip through Tanzania leaves you with memories for the rest of your life. Superb national parks and protected game reserves make up 35% of the country, so a Tanzania safari lets you see nature at its very best. Elephants, lions and countless other wild animals wander the green landscapes, and few spectacles compare to the Great Wildebeest Migration in the Serengeti, where millions of mammals chase the rains in a clockwise loop each year, searching for fresh water and grass.

blocks.orig: Picture grassy plains dotted with grazing animals. Framed with acacia trees and bathed in the warm light of a beautiful African sunset: this is the picture-postcard image that most will associate with Tanzania. Beyond the iconic plains, however, Tanzania’s offers a huge variety of landscapes and adventures. From the savanna to the mighty mountains, from ancient forests bursting with gigantic fig trees to paradisiacal white sandy beaches – a Tanzania travel experience has it all.
blocks.html: Imagine grassy plains scattered with grazing animals, acacia trees on the horizon and the warm glow of a glorious African sunset: this is the postcard scene most people picture when they think of Tanzania. Yet beyond those famous plains, Tanzania holds an enormous range of landscapes and adventures. Savannah and mighty mountains, ancient forests full of giant fig trees, heavenly white-sand beaches – travelling in Tanzania gives you all of it.

blocks.orig: Did you know that Tanzania is home to the most natural wonders of any African country? Three of Africa’s Seven Natural Wonders can be seen in Tanzania. The Great Wildebeest Migration in Tanzania is one of the world’s largest wildlife migrations. To say it’s an impressive sight to see is an understatement. One of the most extraordinary displays of the magnificence of the natural world, millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles thunder across the endless plains of the Serengeti from July to October. Mount Kilimanjaro is another of the three African Wonders in Tanzania, and every year thousands of travellers visit Tanzania with just one goal: to conquer the highest peak of Africa. The last of the three African Natural Wonders in Tanzania is the world’s largest collapsed volcano, the Ngorongoro Crater. It shelters a unique ecosystem and the world’s highest concentration of wildlife per square kilometre.
blocks.html: Did you know that no other African country has as many natural wonders as Tanzania? Three of Africa's Seven Natural Wonders are found here. The Great Wildebeest Migration in Tanzania ranks among the largest wildlife migrations on earth, and calling it impressive hardly does it justice. In one of the most extraordinary displays nature has to offer, millions of wildebeest, zebras and gazelles thunder across the vast plains of the Serengeti between July and October. Mount Kilimanjaro is the second of Tanzania's three African Wonders; every year, thousands of travellers come to Tanzania with a single aim, to reach the highest point in Africa. The third is the Ngorongoro Crater, the largest collapsed volcano in the world, which harbours a unique ecosystem and the highest density of wildlife per square kilometre anywhere on the planet.

blocks.orig: Hungry for adventure? Climb Mount Kilimanjaro!
blocks.html: Craving adventure? Take on Mount Kilimanjaro!

blocks.orig: The mighty Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa (5,895 m / 19,341 ft) and the world’s highest freestanding mountain. Since you don’t need to be an experienced climber to reach its summit, Kilimanjaro is a popular destination for travellers who like to challenge themselves. To conquer the roof of Africa is amazing and truly breathtaking!
blocks.html: Standing at 5,895 m / 19,341 ft, the mighty Mount Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest mountain and the tallest freestanding mountain in the world. You don't have to be a seasoned climber to reach the top, which makes Kilimanjaro a favourite among travellers who enjoy pushing themselves. Standing on the roof of Africa is an incredible, truly breathtaking feeling!

blocks.orig: With more than 120 ethnic groups in the country, Tanzania is one of the most culturally diverse countries in the world. From the graceful Maasai Warriors to the Hadzabe Bushmen, from the Chaga farmers to the Nyamwezi. Each of these groups has different languages, traditions, heritage and culture, some of which you may have the opportunity to engage in during your time in Tanzania. For an immersive cultural experience, ask your Your Tanzania Trip expert for tribal visits and village tours in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Home to more than 120 ethnic groups, Tanzania ranks among the most culturally diverse nations on earth: the graceful Maasai warriors, the Hadzabe bushmen, the Chaga farmers, the Nyamwezi and many more. Each group has its own language, traditions, heritage and culture, and during your stay in Tanzania you may well get the chance to take part in some of them. For a truly immersive cultural experience, ask your Your Tanzania Trip expert about tribal visits and village tours in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Though there are many cultures in Tanzania, the two main languages are Swahili and English. Picking up some key Swahili phrases is a great way to engage with local people during your Tanzania Travel. Throughout Tanzania, you will often hear ‘Jambo’ (hello) or ‘Karibu’ (welcome). If you respond with ‘Nzuri Sana (very good) or ‘Asante Sana (thank you), you’ll be sure to get a warm welcome. Tanzanian people have a lot of respect for elders and are very friendly and polite towards visitors.
blocks.html: Despite the many cultures in Tanzania, the two principal languages are Swahili and English. Learning a few essential Swahili phrases is a lovely way to connect with local people while travelling in Tanzania. Everywhere in the country you'll hear ‘Jambo’ (hello) and ‘Karibu’ (welcome); reply with ‘Nzuri Sana (very good) or ‘Asante Sana (thank you) and a warm welcome is guaranteed. Tanzanians show great respect for their elders and are very friendly and courteous to visitors.

blocks.orig: What makes Tanzanian Travel so popular is that you can combine the adventure of the African bush with an exotic beach holiday. Zanzibar’s white sandy beaches, beautiful coral reefs and azure blue Indian Ocean is everything you need to relax and unwind. Apart from laid back beach life, Zanzibar also has a colourful culture and history. Stone Town is well worth a visit. This fascinating old city offers cool markets, inviting restaurants and plenty of historical sightseeing.
blocks.html: Part of what makes travelling in Tanzania so popular is that the adventure of the African bush can be paired with an exotic beach holiday. The white sandy beaches, beautiful coral reefs and azure blue Indian Ocean of Zanzibar are all you need to switch off and relax. And Zanzibar is more than laid-back beach life: it has a colourful culture and history too. Stone Town deserves a visit, a captivating old city with cool markets, welcoming restaurants and plenty of historic sights.

blocks.orig: Visit Zanzibar, Mafia and Pemba islands and relax after your safari
blocks.html: Unwind after your safari on Zanzibar, Mafia and Pemba islands

blocks.orig: Zanzibar Island is part of the Zanzibar archipelago, together with Pemba Island and Mafia Island and many smaller islands. These islands are also called the Spice Islands because of their rich history in the spice trade and many spice plantations. Zanzibar is a fantastic African beach destination to wash off the dust after your safari!
blocks.html: Zanzibar Island belongs to the Zanzibar archipelago, alongside Pemba Island, Mafia Island and many smaller islands. Thanks to their long history in the spice trade and their many spice plantations, these islands are also known as the Spice Islands. For washing off the dust after your safari, Zanzibar is a fantastic African beach destination!

blocks.orig: Mafia Island is a perfect escape from the fast pace and busy life. This island is still pure and untouched with no tarmac roads and only a few tourists, and many compare it to Zanzibar a few decades ago. Almost half of Mafia’s coastline is part of Mafia Island Marine Park, a nature park, full of coral reefs, mangrove forests and lagoons. A true paradise for divers, snorkellers, and honeymooners.
blocks.html: Mafia Island is the ideal place to escape the rush and bustle of everyday life. Still pure and unspoilt, with no tarmac roads and only a handful of tourists, the island is often likened to Zanzibar a few decades ago. Nearly half of Mafia's coastline falls within Mafia Island Marine Park, a nature park of coral reefs, mangrove forests and lagoons, and a true paradise for divers, snorkellers and honeymooners.

blocks.orig: Pemba Island is a pristine green and truly one of the most beautiful places on the planet. Bursting with forests, mango trees and vast clove plantations, if you are looking for peace and a romantic atmosphere, this is the place to be. For a tranquil hideaway at one of the best dive sites in the world, head to Pemba Island to explore the amazing coral reefs and swim among tropical reef fish.
blocks.html: Pemba Island is unspoilt and green, and genuinely one of the most beautiful spots on earth. Covered in forests, mango trees and vast clove plantations, it is the place to be if you are after peace and a romantic atmosphere. For a tranquil retreat beside one of the world's best dive sites, head to Pemba Island, explore its amazing coral reefs and swim among tropical reef fish.
